claim.pdf_says: The NOTE after General rule 2 of 11.9.6 ('NOTE   NEAREST-AWAY-FROM-ZERO is the rounding mode provided by the ROUNDED phrase in earlier COBOL standards.'), the NOTE after 11.9.7.4 General rule 1 ('NOTE   All information required to interact successfully with a runtime element...'), and sub-items a) and b) under 11.9.7.4 General rule 4 are all printed indented under their parent numbered rule (the NOTEs additionally in the smaller NOTE type size).
claim.markdown_says: All four are transcribed flush at column 0, at the same level as the numbered rules: 'NOTE NEAREST-AWAY-FROM-ZERO is the rounding mode provided by the ROUNDED phrase in earlier COBOL standards.' / 'NOTE All information required to interact successfully with a runtime element can be made available to the compiler via this entry convention association; ...' / 'a) If a class definition includes the INHERITS clause, ...' / 'b) If an interface definition includes the INHERITS clause, ...'
claim.why_it_matters: The NOTEs detach from the rules they qualify and read as free-standing notes of the enclosing subsection, and a)/b) detach from General rule 4 ('When ENTRY-CONVENTION is not specified, the entry convention used is as follows:') so the condition governing them is lost. The same transcription indents these correctly elsewhere (page 172 rule 1 a)-c), page 228 syntax-rule NOTE, page 308 rules 2 a)-e) and its NOTE), so this page departs from the document's own convention.

verdict.reasoning:
Both source descriptions are factually accurate, but the difference is indentation only -- an explicit rejection category (formatting), with no content lost and no meaning changed.

What the PDF actually prints (verified by rendering E:/Temp/specrecon/v304/spec_p304.png at 300 dpi and cropping the two regions at zoom): the '2)' marker of 11.9.6 GR2 sits at the left margin and the NOTE below it begins at the same x as that rule's body text ('If the DEFAULT ROUNDED clause...' / continuation 'FROM-ZERO is implied.'), i.e. one hanging-indent level in, in the smaller NOTE type. Identically, under 11.9.7.4 the 'a)' and 'b)' markers begin at the same x as rule 4's body text ('When ENTRY-CONVENTION is not specified...'), one level in from the '4)' marker, and the NOTE after GR1 is at the body-text level in smaller type. So the claim's reading of the PDF is correct.

What the markdown says (specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 13247-13297): all four lines are at column 0. So the claim's reading of the markdown is correct too.

Why this is not a content discrepancy:
(1) Nothing is missing, added, reordered, or reworded. I compared the full page: header, 11.9.6 GR2 + NOTE, 11.9.7 / .1 / .2 (format diagram + figure note) / .3 SR1 / .4 GR1-4 with both NOTEs and a)/b) are all present verbatim and in printed reading order. The only omissions are page furniture (printed page number 274, copyright line, license footer), which is out of scope.
(2) The hierarchy survives without the indent because it is carried redundantly by the enumerators themselves. The top-level list is numeric ('1)'..'4)'); the sub-items are alphabetic ('a)', 'b)'). An alphabetic item cannot be misread as a member of a numeric list, and it appears immediately after a rule that ends in the colon 'the entry convention used is as follows:'. The governing condition of rule 4 is therefore not lost -- it is the immediately preceding line, exactly as in the PDF.
(3) The NOTEs likewise keep their attachment by position and by the literal 'NOTE' label. The 11.9.7.4 NOTE sits between rule 1) and rule 2) in the markdown, precisely where the PDF prints it, so it still reads as annotating rule 1. The 11.9.6 NOTE follows GR2, which is the terminal rule of that subsection's rule list, so 'note to rule 2' and 'note at the end of 11.9.6' have the same practical scope; and NOTEs are informative, not normative (ISO/IEC Directives Part 2), so no normative statement changes scope either way.

The one durable observation in the claim is a house-style inconsistency, and I confirmed it: page 172 (GR1 a)-c)), page 228 (SR1's NOTE) and page 308 (GR2 a)-e) + NOTE, GR3 a)-b)) all use a 3-space indent for subordinate items, while page 304 uses column 0 for all four. That is a cosmetic normalization nit worth a cleanup pass, not a structural content defect, and it does not rise to the 'genuine content discrepancy' bar.
verdict.corrected_description: REFUTED as a content discrepancy; accurate only as a cosmetic style inconsistency. The claim's factual observations about both sources check out -- the PDF prints the two NOTEs and sub-items a)/b) one hanging-indent level in (NOTEs in the smaller NOTE type), and the markdown puts all four at column 0. But no text is missing, altered or reordered, and no meaning is lost: subordination is carried by the enumerator style (alphabetic a)/b) under a numeric 1)-4) list), by rule 4's trailing 'as follows:' colon, by the 'NOTE' label, and by unchanged reading order; NOTEs are informative under ISO/IEC Directives Part 2, and the 11.9.6 NOTE follows that subsection's terminal rule so its scope is unchanged in either reading. The correct, downgraded finding is: 'page 304 does not apply the transcription's own 3-space subordinate-item indent (cf. pages 172, 228, 308)' -- kind=formatting-inconsistency, severity=cosmetic.
